# FANUC TP / LS language references

The source editor uses an independent TypeScript LS structural parser, now cross-checked against the accessible FANUC-authored Basic **B-83284EN/09** and Optional **B-83284EN-2/09** manuals. See [COVERAGE.md](COVERAGE.md) for the chapter-by-chapter implementation gaps. It preserves source and reports unsupported forms; it is not a FANUC compiler, controller emulator, or a verified complete grammar. Catalog descriptions and test programs are newly authored. Original MIT notices accompany the two repositories inspected during research; their licenses do not apply to FANUC manuals or imply FANUC approval.

The fixed fanuc-lsp source is useful for instruction-family cross-checking but explicitly omits general multi-group positions, some program subtypes and POINT_LOGIC options. Its motion-speed parser accepts AR[] although the independent v9.40+ reference states indirect motion speed must first use R[]. Its ALIM option is not integrated in dispatch. These issues are not inherited as authoritative grammar rules.

The implementation parses file sections, statement framing, expressions, reference indirection, motion arguments, IF/FOR/SELECT nesting, calls, labels, common register/IO forms and repeated motion groups in P definitions. Cartesian CONFIG, joint positions, external axes and uninitialized coordinates remain distinct. Undefined local labels are errors; undefined program positions are warnings because they can still be awaiting teaching. Calls/macros, dynamic register values, system-variable existence, I/O wiring, group kinematics and application-option behavior cannot be confirmed from one source file.

The metadata explicitly marks v9.40+ LOCAL_REGISTERS and application-specific instructions. Unknown statements/options are kept and diagnosed, never converted to no-ops. Binary TP conversion requires an appropriate vendor toolchain or controller ASCII Upload; LS text export alone is not proof of controller compatibility.

`tests/programming-fanuc.test.ts` uses authored positive/negative examples of the documented forms, including multiline circular moves, both SELECT representations, GP1+GP2/external axes, nested references, malformed control flow and resource limits. These are structural regression checks, not official compiler conformance results.

The manuals were obtained from a pinned public mirror, not an official FANUC host. Their hashes and byte sizes are recorded in SOURCE.json; copyrighted PDFs and extracted contents remain outside the repository. Access to the Basic manual is not a blocker. Basic application trees (CONFIG/BOTTOM/PATTERN/ROUTE), circular passing-point options and statically decidable operand types are now parsed. Specific unresolved ASCII evidence remains for nonempty POINT_LOGIC child data, E/EX all-point arrangement enum spelling and auxiliary bottom-point keys. The manual documents the corresponding pendant workflow but does not establish those serialized tokens. A real LS export containing those features is required; the original source is preserved and diagnosed meanwhile. The chapter audit also tracks remaining compatibility combinations and application profiles independently of binary compilation or execution.
